units.function: Registry, built-in GitHub provider and persistence-service tests for sanitized external-object detection, company-scoped identity, status snapshots, refresh scheduling/fencing, mention sync and plugin-backed providers.
units.dependencyDirection: Vitest -> detector/resolver registries and GitHub provider -> external-object service -> Drizzle/PostgreSQL; built-in HTTP is mocked and plugin calls use a fake worker manager, so real network, credential provider and worker isolation are outside the unit.
units.keyDataModels: Canonical URL/hash, ExternalObject, ExternalObjectMention/source context, provider/object/external IDs, structured status/liveness/error/TTL/ETag, refresh token/start/next time, company status and plugin manifest/capabilities.
units.lifecycle: Extract and sanitize URLs -> provider-first detect or generic fallback -> upsert company-scoped object/mention -> schedule due refresh -> claim/fence resolver work -> persist snapshot or safe failure while retaining last good status -> skip paused companies/terminal objects -> remove deleted-source mentions.
units.testAssessment: Fourteen pure tests passed and twelve embedded-Postgres tests skipped in both sandboxed and approved unsandboxed runs. Source coverage includes unusually good concurrent refresh replacement and stale-writer fencing, but no real database behavior, network policy, plugin isolation or credential boundary executed on the audit host.
units.designRationale: Keep raw secret-bearing URLs out of storage, let providers own typed detection before a generic link fallback, separate business status from reachability, preserve useful stale state during outages and coordinate refreshes across processes with a replaceable claimant token.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS requires enterprise DataReferences and snapshots that are tenant-owned, provenance-rich, safely refreshed through equal Connectors and governed by purpose/data/export contracts rather than being ambient links found in Work text.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT canonical sanitization, provider registry, company-scoped identity, structured liveness/status, last-good snapshot, safe error codes, scheduled refresh and database fencing. Reframe detectors/resolvers as DataConnector capabilities under DataAuthorization; define provider-specific identity normalization, immutable provenance/snapshot digests, retention, size/time/network budgets, approval-aware refresh and explicit terminal revalidation policy.
units.responsibilityConflict: The service records source mentions and company context but no accountable human, Work purpose, ResponsibilityContract, DataAuthorization, approval or immutable access receipt. An installed plugin with declared capabilities is treated as a provider without this unit proving tenant consent or data/credential scope.
evidence: 2026-08-19 sandboxed focused Vitest: 14/14 pure passed, 12/12 embedded-Postgres skipped
2026-08-19 approved unsandboxed focused Vitest: 14/14 pure passed, 12/12 embedded-Postgres skipped
units.securityFindings: CRITICAL plugin/data authority gap if reused directly: declared detect/read capabilities are not shown to enforce tenant consent, DataAuthorization, credential or egress scope. HIGH network hardening gap: timeout, redirect/DNS behavior, response-size/schema abuse and cancellation are untested. HIGH identity-normalization risk: universally removing query parameters can merge distinct enterprise resources. HIGH evidence gap: no immutable snapshot/access receipt or purpose binding. MEDIUM lifecycle gap: terminal objects never auto-refresh and orphan object retention is untested. MEDIUM distributed-scheduler gap: clock skew, crash/restart and fairness are absent. MEDIUM verification gap: all 12 database tests skipped locally.
